Ministry of MSME and Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation Sign Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for development and strengthening of the Statistical Business Register
articles.full_content:
MoU will facilitate structured framework for sharing relevant information from Udyam Registration ecosystem
A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) has been exchanged between Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), to institutionalize a mechanism for sharing relevant data for the development and strengthening of the Statistical Business Register (SBR).
The MoU was signed by Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner, Ministry of MSME and Dr. Dalip Singh, Additional Director General, MoSPI, in the presence of senior officers from Ministry of MSME and MoSPI.
Objectives of the MoU:-
-The MoU sets the terms and understanding between the Ministry of MSME and MoSPI in relation to the sharing of unit-wise data of the Udyam Registration available with MSME Department through APIs. The two-way API shall provide data for preparation of National Statistical Business Register (NSBR).
-The MoU will facilitate a structured framework for sharing relevant information from the Udyam Registration ecosystem of the Ministry of MSME with MoSPI. The information will contribute to improving the coverage, consistency and reliability of business information used for statistical purposes.
Statistical Business Register (SBR): An Overview
-The Statistical Business Register (SBR) is a central and regularly updated database of registered statistical units engaged in economic activities within a defined geographical territory. It captures businesses, enterprises, establishments & other relevant economic units, key characteristics of economic units and relationships between different units.
- The SBR serves as foundational infrastructure for the economic statistics system to improve the coverage, consistency and reliability of business information by identifying the target population for economic surveys, supporting survey sample selection, enabling the production of business demography statistics, providing a common framework for business demography-related information, and facilitating integration and consistency across different data sources.

Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Prepares for Special Campaign 6 building on Strong Outcomes Achieved under Special Campaign 5.0
articles.full_content:
The Government of India has announced the launch of Special Campaign 6, to be conducted from 2nd–31st October 2026, with the preparatory phase from 15th–30th September 2026. The campaign will focus on institutionalising cleanliness in Government offices, disposal of pending references, efficient record management, e-waste management, effective space utilisation and enhancing workplace experience.
The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) actively participated in Special Campaign 5.0 with a strong emphasis on cleanliness, records management, space optimisation and disposal of pending references across its offices and institutions. During the campaign, more than 1,836 cleanliness drives were conducted. The Ministry disposed of 3 references from Members of Parliament, 7 Parliament Assurances, 307 Public Grievances and 27 Public Grievance Appeals .
As part of the record management initiatives, 1,250 files were reviewed and 466 files were weeded out . In addition, 658 e-files were reviewed, out of which 266 e-files were closed . These efforts resulted in freeing approximately 4,000 square feet of office space through weeding out of files and disposal of scrap. The disposal of scrap also generated revenue of approximately ₹7.58 lakh .
The collective efforts of MSDE and its attached, autonomous, subordinate and field offices contributed towards creating cleaner and more efficient workplaces, improving record management and optimising available office space. The campaign also strengthened awareness regarding the importance of maintaining a clean office environment and responsible disposal of waste.
In preparation for Special Campaign 6, MSDE has initiated preparatory activities and is coordinating with the nodal officers and stakeholders of its attached, subordinate and autonomous organisations and field institutions. The nodal officers are being sensitised regarding the key focus areas of the campaign, including cleanliness, disposal of pending references, efficient record management, e-waste management in accordance with the applicable E-Waste Management Rules, 2022, space management and enhancement of workplace experience.
The Ministry is committed to carrying forward the momentum generated during Special Campaign 5.0 and contributing significantly to the objectives of Special Campaign 6 through sustainable cleanliness practices, effective disposal of pendency, responsible e-waste management, improved record management and creation of cleaner, more efficient and better-utilised workspaces.

The campaign will focus on institutionalising cleanliness in Government offices, disposal of pending references, efficient record management, e-waste management, effective space utilisation and enhancing workplace experience. The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) actively participated in Special Campaign 5.0 with a strong emphasis on cleanliness, records management, space optimisation and disposal of pending references across its offices and institutions.

Ministry of Mines Strengthens E-Waste Collection Drive under Special Campaign 6 to Promote Circular Economy and Critical Mineral Recovery
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Mines, Government of India, is strengthening its E-Waste Collection Campaign under Special Campaign 6 with a focus on responsible e-waste management, resource recovery and promotion of a circular economy.
The campaign is being coordinated and implemented through the Jawaharlal Nehru Aluminium Research Development and Design Centre (JNARDDC), Nagpur, designated as the Nodal Agency for the campaign, in association with the Material Recycling Association of India (MRAI). Collection and awareness activities are being undertaken at multiple locations by offices and organisations associated with the Ministry of Mines.
More than 44 office locations across the country have been finalised for the campaign. In Maharashtra alone, more than 28 locations have been identified for e-waste collection. The widespread participation of offices and organisations reflects the coordinated efforts being undertaken to promote responsible collection and disposal of e-waste. The Ministry of Mines office in New Delhi is also one of the identified collection locations under the campaign. E-waste collected at various participating locations will be channelised for responsible recycling and resource recovery through appropriate mechanisms.
E-waste is not merely a waste stream but also a potential source of valuable secondary resources. With several electronic products containing minerals and metals that are important for modern technologies, recycling and recovery from e-waste can contribute to resource efficiency and strengthen the circular economy for critical minerals. Responsible recycling can help recover valuable materials, reduce pressure on primary mineral resources and promote sustainable utilisation of resources.
As part of the preparatory activities for effective implementation of the campaign, JNARDDC has conducted virtual coordination meetings with designated Nodal Officers of various offices and organisations under the Ministry of Mines, including the Geological Survey of India (GSI), Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM), National Institute of Rock Mechanics (NIRM), National Aluminium Company Limited (NALCO), Hindustan Zinc Limited (HZL), Mineral Exploration and Consultancy Limited (MECL) and Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL).
The Ministry and its field offices and organisations are also undertaking awareness activities, campaigns and competitions to encourage greater participation among employees and stakeholders. These activities aim to promote awareness about responsible e-waste disposal and encourage reuse, repurposing and recycling of discarded electronic and electrical products, wherever feasible.
Through the campaign, the Ministry is promoting Jan Bhagidari in resource conservation and encouraging responsible practices for the collection, segregation, recycling and recovery of materials from e-waste. NITI Aayog launches Special Campaign 6.0 to institutionalise Swachhata and minimising pendency
articles.full_content:
With the vision of paying a heartfelt tribute of “A Clean India” to Mahatma Gandhi, the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) initiated a special campaign for disposal of pending matters in 2021. Building upon the success of the campaign, DARPG decided to continue the campaign in 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and further in 2026. Accordingly, Special Campaign 5.0 was undertaken from November 2025 to August 2026 with the aim of ensuring timely and effective disposal of public grievances, references from Members of Parliament, State Governments, Inter-Ministerial Consultations and Parliamentary Assurances by Ministries/Departments.
Special Campaign 5.0 for disposal of pending matters and Swachhta was undertaken by NITI Aayog and its attached offices Development Monitoring & Evaluation Office (DMEO), Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) located in NITI Bhawan and its autonomous institution viz. National Institute of Labour Economics Research and Development (NILERD) situated in Narela, New Delhi.
During the campaign, disposal of Public Grievances, Parliamentary Assurances and PMO References have gained momentum. NITI Aayog had successfully disposed of 4,105 Public Grievances, 127 PMO references, 34 Public Grievance Appeals and 05 Parliamentary Assurances. In addition to the above, approximately 90 sqft. of space was freed by way of disposal of files and optimisation of office space. A total revenue of Rs. 1,96,905/- was realised by way of scrap disposal.
In line with the success of previous years, NITI Aayog is gearing up for Special Campaign 6.0 with the objective of institutionalising Swachhata and minimising pendency in the Secretariat as well as attached /subordinate offices. In this edition of the campaign, focus shall be on liquidating pendency in the MP’s References, References from the State Governments, Inter-Ministerial References, Parliamentary Assurances, PMO references, Public Grievances and PG Appeals and weeding out of redundant files & documents. In addition, special attention shall be given to improving the overall cleanliness of the offices with a focus on space management and enhancing workplace experience of field offices.

Assam Launches Comprehensive Multi-Agency Strategy to Implement Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026
articles.full_content:
Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 come into force with effect from April 1, 2026 Four-Stream Segregation of Solid Waste at Source Made Mandatory; Clear Responsibilities Defined for Bulk Waste Generators
Key Features of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026
• SWM Rules, 2026 supersede the 2016 Rules and come into force from April 1, 2026 .
• Four-stream segregation at source—wet, dry, sanitary and special care waste—is mandatory.
• Bulk Waste Generators must ensure environmentally sound collection, transportation and processing, with Extended Bulk Waste Generator Responsibility (EBWGR) introduced.
• Environmental compensation will apply under the Polluter Pays principle for non-compliance.
• A Centralised Online Portal will enable end-to-end monitoring, registration, reporting and audits.
• MRFs (Material Recovery Facilities) are formally recognised for waste sorting.
• Landfilling is restricted to non-recyclable, non-energy-recoverable and inert waste .
• Legacy dumpsites will undergo time-bound biomining and bioremediation .
• Special provisions cover hilly areas and islands , including tourist user fees and decentralised waste management.
The Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has notified the Solid Waste Management (SWM) Rules, 2026, under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 which came into effect from April 1, 2026. In this regard, a joint press conference was held by the Assam Pollution Control Board, Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban) and Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin), Assam today.
Dr. Arup Kumar Mishra, Chairman of Pollution Control Board Assam, delivered an elaborate address on the statutory framework of the rules and the progress of its implementation in Assam. Dr. Mishra emphasized that waste management is no longer the exclusive mandate of pollution control boards, but a collective operational duty for all local bodies, institutions and citizens. Highlighting recent directives from the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Bhopal Municipal Corporation v. Dr. Subhash C. Pandey & Ors . (Civil Appeal No. 6174 of 2023), Dr. Mishra noted that the court's mandates now apply nationwide to all twenty-eight State Pollution Control Boards. He explained that while materials like plastics and discarded tires have historically created major environmental menaces, the 2026 framework strictly prioritizes avoiding landfills and treating organic biodegradable waste as a valuable resource.
Elaborating further on the operational mandates, Dr. Mishra highlighted the foundational requirement of four-stream waste segregation at source, requiring every household, establishment and institutional generator to store wet biodegradable waste, dry recyclables, securely wrapped sanitary waste and special care waste—such as CFL bulbs, expired medicines, batteries, tube lights, and syringes—in separate containers before handing them over to authorized collectors. The index is compiled with data received from source agencies, which in turn receive the data from the producing factories/ establishments. These Quick Estimates will undergo revision in subsequent releases as per the revision policy of IIP.

• The growth rates of the sectors, Mining & Quarrying, Manufacturing, Electricity & Gas Supply and Water Supply, Sewerage & Waste Management for the month of August 2026 are (-) 5.6 percent, 9.0 percent, 12.3 percent and 6.3 percent respectively.
• The Quick Estimate of IIP stands at 123.3 against 114.2 in August 2025. The indices of Industrial Production for Mining & Quarrying, Manufacturing, Electricity & Gas Supply and Water Supply, Sewerage & Waste Management for the month of August 2026 stand at 85.7, 126.6, 133.9 and 147.6 respectively.
• Within the Manufacturing sector, 18 out of 23 industry groups at NIC 2 digit-level have recorded a positive growth in August 2026 over August 2025. NITI Aayog Member Dr. Joram Aniya Visits BRIC-IBSD Imphal; Highlights Indigenous Knowledge for Viksit Bharat 2047
articles.full_content:
Dr. Joram Aniya, Member, NITI Aayog, visited the BRIC-Institute of Bioresources and Sustainable Development (BRIC-IBSD), Imphal, on Monday and delivered a Societal Development Lecture on “Indigenous Knowledge Systems and Viksit Bharat 2047” as the Special Guest. The lecture focused on the relevance of indigenous knowledge systems and their role in advancing India’s vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. The programme began with the felicitation of the Special Guest and the invitees, followed by a lamp lighting ceremony and the rendition of the national song, Vande Mataram.
In the welcome address, Dr Nanaocha Sharma, Director (Addl. Charge), BRIC-IBSD, highlighted the Institute's efforts to bridge traditional knowledge and modern scientific research in Northeast India, a region of exceptional biological diversity and rich indigenous knowledge. Dr R.K. Radhesana Devi, Director, Planning Department, Government of Manipur, and Dr R.K. Tombisana Singh, Joint Director, Planning Department, Government of Manipur, were among the dignitaries present.
During the programme, the Special Guest released A Compendium on Medicinal Plants of the Family Zingiberaceae from North-East India (Volume-I) , edited by Dr Ch. Brajakishor Singh, Dr H. Sunitabala Devi, Dr Biseshwori Th, and Dr Nanaocha Sharma, and published by BRIC-IBSD. The Compendium compiles documented information on the medicinal plants of the ginger family from the region.
In her address, Dr Aniya spoke on indigenous knowledge systems and underscored the importance of nature, the environment and biotechnological research. She also emphasised the role of research institutions in realising the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. The programme concluded with a vote of thanks by Dr J.K. Shukla, Scientist, BRIC-IBSD. Dr Aniya subsequently visited the Institute's Genome Sequencing Facility.

The lecture focused on the relevance of indigenous knowledge systems and their role in advancing India’s vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. The programme began with the felicitation of the Special Guest and the invitees, followed by a lamp lighting ceremony and the rendition of the national song, Vande Mataram.

Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman will embark on an official visit to Qatar from 27 th to 29 th September, 2026. The Union Finance Minister is leading the delegation comprising of Ministry of Finance officials.
During the visit, Smt. Sitharaman will attend the 11 th Annual Meeting of Board of Governors of Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) scheduled in Doha on 28 th September 2026, besides other important bilateral meetings with the AIIB President and her counterparts from Jordan, Switzerland, Algeria, Saudi Arabia, and Nepal.
In the Annual Meeting of AIIB, the Union Finance Minister will attend as the Indian Governor to the AIIB. India is the second largest shareholder of the bank.
As part of the official visit, the Union Finance Minister is expected to call-on the leadership of the Government of Qatar, and also engage with Qatari business leaders and investors.
About AIIB and Annual Meetings
The AIIB Annual Meeting witnesses participation of delegations from member countries, and other international organisations. As a multilateral development bank, AIIB is focused on developing sustainable infrastructure in Asia and in promoting investments in infrastructure and other productive sectors with the aim to foster sustainable economic development, create wealth and improve infrastructure connectivity.

Sitharaman will also hold important bilateral meetings with the AIIB President and her counterparts including from Jordan, Switzerland, Algeria, Saudi Arabia, and Nepal Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman will embark on an official visit to Qatar from 27 th to 29 th September, 2026.
